title: Longest Safe Path (Allow One Blocker)
statement:
You are given a string made of lowercase English letters and `#` characters. A `#` is a **blocker**.

In the warm-up version of this problem a *safe path* is a contiguous substring that contains no `#` at all, and you return the longest one. The twist this problem asks about is the follow-up: **one blocker is allowed to be treated as safe**. A safe path is now a contiguous substring that contains **at most one** `#`.

Return the longest safe path. If several substrings share the maximum length, return the one that starts **earliest** in the string. The answer is the substring itself (it may contain a single `#`).

For example, in `ab##cde#fghij` the blocker-free segments have lengths `2, 0, 3, 5`; with one blocker allowed you can take `cde#fghij`, of length 9.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string (no spaces).
outputFormat: Print the longest safe path as a string.
constraints: `s` consists of lowercase English letters and `#`

examples.explanation: `ab#cdef` has exactly one `#` and length 7. Extending it to the right would include the second `#` of `##`, and no other window with at most one `#` is longer than 7.
The window `cde#fghij` contains one `#` and has length 9, which beats every other valid window.
Any window of length 2 or 3 contains at least two `#`. The longest valid windows have length 1; the earliest one starts at index 0.

hints: Think of a window `[left, right]` that you slide to the right one character at a time.
Keep a count of `#` characters in the window. When the count exceeds one, advance `left` until it is back to at most one.
Only record a new best window when it is strictly longer than the previous best; that gives the earliest start on ties.
